# All Nobel Prizes in Physics

The Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded 120 times to 231 Nobel Prize laureates between 1901 and 2026. John Bardeen is the only laureate who has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, in 1956 and 1972. This means that a total of 230 individuals have received the Nobel Prize in Physics. > “for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”

[Pierre Agostini](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/agostini/facts/), [Ferenc Krausz](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/krausz/facts/) and [Anne L’Huillier](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/lhuillier/facts/)

[Alain Aspect](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2022/aspect/facts/), [John Clauser](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2022/clauser/facts/) and [Anton Zeilinger](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2022/zeilinger/facts/)

> “for experiments with entangled photons, establishing the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneering quantum information science”

> “for groundbreaking contributions to our understanding of complex physical systems”

Bohr is a lunar impact crater that is located along the western lunar limb, in the area that is affected by librations . [ 3 ] It is attached to the southwestern rim of the larger, eroded Vasco da Gama formation, and to the southeast of the degrade Bohr (crater) - Wikipedia The rim to the northeast has been shored up by the adjacent Vasco da Gama, but the remainder forms an irregular ring of rugged ground. To the southwest of Bohr is Vallis Bohr , a valley trending in a north–south direction. [ 5 ] This long cleft is associated with the formation of the Mare Orientale farther to the south. [ 6 ]

Lenard ( Moon )

Named after Philipp Edward Anton Lenard - German physicist, 1905 Nobel Prize winner for physics (1862-1947).

Lenard is a lunar impact crater located on the lunar far side near the northern pole. The crater forms some of the wall of the crater Hermite , and is located North of the craters Lovelace and Froelich . ( wikipedia entry ) ## Lenard ([Moon](/world/moon))

#### Named after [Philipp Edward Anton Lenard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philipp_Lenard) - German physicist, 1905 Nobel Prize winner for physics (1862-1947).

#### Lenard is a lunar impact crater located on the lunar far side near the northern pole. The crater forms some of the wall of the crater [Hermite](/feature/2471#Hermite.14503), and is located North of the craters [Lovelace](/feature/3488#Lovelace.14503) and [Froelich](/feature/2030#Froelich.14503). ([wikipedia entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenard_(crater)))

Every named place on the Moon

2,023 features carry an official name, and for every one of them the International Astronomical Union wrote down why .
